1: Because of the affliction by the threefold suffering, inquiry arises into the cause that removes that affliction,
2: if in the seen (empirical means) it is thought purposeless, since there is no absolute and final cessation therein // ISk_1 //
3: Like the seen, what is based on <s>ānuśravika</s> (scriptural tradition) is indeed impure, marked by decay and excess,
4: its opposite is better, as it rests on discriminative knowledge of the manifest and the unmanifest // ISk_2 //
5: The root <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) is unmodified; beginning with the <s>Mahad</s> (great principle) the seven are both <s>prakṛti</s> (source) and <s>vikṛti</s> (product),
6: but the sixteen are products; and the <s>Puruṣa</s> (self) is neither <s>prakṛti</s> nor <s>vikṛti</s> // ISk_3 //
7: Perception, inference, and the word of a trustworthy authority are accepted, since all means of knowledge are established (as such),
8: threefold knowledge-means are approved; for the establishment of the knowables is from the means of knowledge // ISk_4 //
9: Perception is a determinate apprehension with respect to its object; threefold inference is declared,
10: that (inference) being preceded by the mark and the marked; and the trustworthy hearing is indeed authoritative testimony // ISk_5 //
11: From what is generally perceived, the apprehension of things beyond the senses is through inference,
12: and even that which is not (thus) established, being remote, is to be proved by the authoritative scripture of the trustworthy // ISk_6 //
13: Because of too great distance, because of proximity, because of injury to the senses, because of unsteadiness of mind,
14: because of subtlety, because of interposition, because of overpowering, and because of mingling with what is similar // ISk_7 //
15: Because of subtlety, the non-apprehension of that is not due to non-existence; its apprehension is from its effect,
16: the <s>Mahad</s> and what follows are that effect; and it is both unlike and like to <s>Prakṛti</s> // ISk_8 //
17: Because the non-existent does not produce, because of the taking up of material cause, because of the absence of everything’s arising from everything,
18: because the capable produces what can be produced, and because of the state of cause, the effect exists (pre-exists) // ISk_9 //
19: The sign (mark) is accompanied by a cause, impermanent, non-pervasive, active, manifold, dependent,
20: composite, relative to another; the manifest is such; the unmanifest is the opposite // ISk_10 //
21: The manifest is three-<s>guṇa</s> (constituted of three qualities), non-discriminating, an object, general, non-conscious, possessing the nature of production,
22: so also is the <s>Pradhāna</s> (<s>Prakṛti</s> as the chief cause); and the opposite of that is likewise the <s>Pumān</s> (<s>Puruṣa</s>) // ISk_11 //
23: The <s>guṇa</s>s have the activities of mutual overpowering, support, generation, and pairing with one another,
24: their natures being pleasure, pain, and delusion, and their purposes being illumination, activity, and restraint // ISk_12 //
25: <s>Sattva</s> is light, illuminating, and desirable; <s>Rajas</s> is mobile and supports (the others);
26: <s>Tamas</s> is heavy and veiling; and function is according to the object, like a lamp // ISk_13 //
27: The unmanifest is established because of the tri-<s>guṇa</s> nature, because of the absence of the reversal of that,
28: and because the effect is of the nature of the cause’s qualities; thus even the unmanifest is established // ISk_14 //
29: From the limitedness of differences, from the convergence (coherence), from the fact of activity according to power,
30: from the division of cause and effect, and from the non-division (continuity) of the universal form // ISk_15 //
31: The unmanifest cause exists; it operates because of the three <s>guṇa</s>s and because of their aggregation,
32: because of transformation, like water, and because of particularity according to the substratum of each <s>guṇa</s> in turn // ISk_16 //
33: Because a composite is for the sake of another, because of the inversion (contrast) with the three <s>guṇa</s>s, and because of a governing basis,
34: <s>Puruṣa</s> exists, because of being an enjoyer, and because of activity aimed at isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) // ISk_17 //
35: From the regulation of birth, death, and instruments (organs), and because they do not operate simultaneously,
36: the multiplicity of <s>Puruṣa</s> is established, and also because of the contrariety to the tri-<s>guṇa</s> // ISk_18 //
37: And from that contrariety, the witnesshood of this <s>Puruṣa</s> is established,
38: isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>), neutrality, seership, and the state of non-agency // ISk_19 //
39: Therefore, from the conjunction with that (Puruṣa), the non-conscious mark-body (<s>liṅga</s>, subtle body) appears as if conscious,
40: and though the <s>guṇa</s>s are the agents, thus he (Puruṣa), being indifferent, seems as if the doer // ISk_20 //
41: For the sake of the vision of the <s>Puruṣa</s>, and for the sake of isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) of <s>Pradhāna</s>,
42: the conjunction of both, like the lame and the blind, occurs; from that is produced creation // ISk_21 //
43: From <s>Prakṛti</s> comes the <s>Mahān</s> (Great Principle); from that the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle); from that the group of sixteen,
44: and from this very sixteen, from the five, the five elements arise // ISk_22 //
45: Determination is <s>buddhi</s> (intellect); virtue, knowledge, dispassion, and lordliness are (its) forms when <s>sāttvika</s>,
46: the opposite of these from it is <s>tāmasa</s> (their perversion) // ISk_23 //
47: Self-appropriation is <s>ahaṅkāra</s>; from that twofold creation proceeds,
48: the elevenfold of the senses, and the pentad of subtle elements (<s>tanmātra</s>) // ISk_24 //
49: The elevenfold, being <s>sāttvika</s>, proceeds from the modified <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (<s>vaikṛta</s>),
50: the subtle element from the <s>bhūta</s>-type (elemental) is <s>tāmasa</s>; from the <s>taijasa</s> (rajasic) are both // ISk_25 //
51: The knowledge-senses (<s>buddhīndriya</s>) are those called ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose,
52: speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals are said to be the action-senses (<s>karmendriya</s>) // ISk_26 //
53: Here the mind (<s>manas</s>) is of a dual nature, being both deliberative (saṅkalpaka) and, by similarity, an organ (indriya),
54: manifoldness (of the senses) is due to the specific transformations of the <s>guṇa</s>s, and also because of the diversity of what is to be apprehended // ISk_27 //
55: For the five (knowledge-senses), with respect to forms and the rest (rūpa, etc.), the function is held to be mere illumination (āloka) alone,
56: but for the five (action-senses) the functions are speech, taking, moving about (enjoyment), evacuation, and procreation (delight) // ISk_28 //
57: By their own particular marks (svālakṣaṇa), the function of the three (inner organs) is this distinctive (asāmānya) one,
58: whereas the function of the general organs (i.e., the senses as common instruments) is (carried by) the five breaths, beginning with <s>Prāṇa</s>; these are the five winds // ISk_29 //
59: And the function of the fourfold set (of inner organs together with vital winds) occurs simultaneously, and also for that (set) a sequential operation is stated,
60: similarly in the seen and in the unseen; for the three (inner organs) the function is preceded by that (viz., by the operation of the senses) // ISk_30 //
61: Each takes up its own respective function, whose cause is one another’s prompting (mutual instigation),
62: only the purpose of the <s>Puruṣa</s> is the cause; no instrument does anything by (its own) agency // ISk_31 //
63: The instrument (karaṇa) is of thirteen kinds; it effects taking in, holding, and illumination,
64: and its product (kārya) is tenfold: what is to be taken in, to be held, and to be illuminated // ISk_32 //
65: The inner instrument is threefold; the outer is tenfold, named the objects of the three (sets of senses),
66: the external instrument operates in the present time, the internal instrument operates across the three times (past, present, future) // ISk_33 //
67: Of these, the five knowledge-senses have as their objects the particular and the non-particular (the specific and the generic),
68: speech has sound as its object; the remaining (action-senses) too have five (kinds of) objects // ISk_34 //
69: Because the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), along with the inner instrument, apprehends every object,
70: therefore the instrument is threefold (within), while the others are the doors; at the doorway (they stand) // ISk_35 //
71: These specific modes of the <s>guṇa</s>s, distinct from one another, are like lamps,
72: having illuminated the entire purpose of the <s>Puruṣa</s>, they deliver it to the intellect // ISk_36 //
73: Since the intellect accomplishes for the <s>Puruṣa</s> all experiential enjoyment,
74: that very intellect discriminates thereafter the subtle difference between <s>Pradhāna</s> (<s>Prakṛti</s>) and <s>Puruṣa</s> // ISk_37 //
75: The subtle elements (<s>tanmātra</s>) are the non-particulars; from these arise the five gross elements (<s>bhūta</s>),
76: these are remembered as the particulars (viśeṣa), and they are serene, terrible, and dull (threefold) // ISk_38 //
77: The particulars are threefold: subtle (innate), born of mother and father, and together with the powerful (supernormal) ones,
78: of these, the subtle are fixed; those born of mother and father cease (at death) // ISk_39 //
79: The subtle mark-body (<s>liṅga</s>), produced earlier, unattached, determinate, extending from the <s>Mahad</s> down to the subtlest,
80: wanders, devoid of enjoyment, perfumed by dispositions (bhāva), through transmigration // ISk_40 //
81: Variegated (experience), apart from its support, exists no more than shade without a post or the like,
82: so too, without the particulars, the <s>liṅga</s> does not remain unsupported // ISk_41 //
83: This (liṅga) is for the sake of the <s>Puruṣa</s>’s purpose, and through the connection of occasional cause and occasioned,
84: because of the pervasiveness-capacity of <s>Prakṛti</s>, it stands forth like an actor // ISk_42 //
85: And innate attainments (sāṃsiddhika) and natural, as well as modified, qualities such as virtue and the rest,
86: are observed resting on the instruments, and the effects such as embryo and the rest rest on (material) products // ISk_43 //
87: By virtue (dharma) there is upward going; by vice (adharma) there is downward going,
88: by knowledge there is release (<s>apavarga</s>), and bondage is held to be through error (viparyaya) // ISk_44 //
89: By dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) there is dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s>; samsara arises from <s>Rajas</s> through passion (rāga),
90: by lordly power (<s>aiśvarya</s>) there is unobstructedness, and through its contrary there is the opposite of that // ISk_45 //
91: This is the projection of cognitions (pratyaya-sarga), named error, incapacity, satisfaction, and success,
92: through the mutual clash of inequality of the <s>guṇa</s>s; and its divisions are fifty // ISk_46 //
93: The five are divisions of error, and of incapacity because of the defectiveness of the instruments,
94: satisfaction has twenty-eight divisions, and success is eightfold // ISk_47 //
95: Error (tamas) has eight divisions, delusion (moha) ten, and great delusion (mahāmoha),
96: <s>Tāmisra</s> is eighteenfold, and likewise is <s>Andhatāmisra</s> // ISk_48 //
97: The incapacity is stated as the impairments of the eleven senses together with impairments of the intellect,
98: there are seventeen impairments of the intellect; satisfaction and success arise from error’s (removal/contrary) // ISk_49 //
99: And the four internal satisfactions are called nature (prakṛti), material cause (upādāna), time, and fortune,
100: the external satisfactions are said to be nine, five from the cessation of objects and (in all) nine // ISk_50 //
101: Conjecture (ūha), authoritative word (śabda), study (adhyayana), the triple removal of suffering, obtaining a friend,
102: and giving (dāna) are the eight successes; prior to success is a threefold goad (spur) of success // ISk_51 //
103: Without dispositions (<s>bhāva</s>), the subtle mark-body (<s>liṅga</s>) does not (come to) be, and without the subtle mark-body (<s>liṅga</s>) there is no accomplishment (occurrence) of dispositions (<s>bhāva</s>),
104: therefore the projection (creation) is twofold, called subtle mark-body (<s>liṅga</s>-named) and disposition (<s>bhāva</s>-named) // ISk_52 //
105: The divine (birth) is eightfold in its varieties, and the animal womb is fivefold,
106: and the human is of a single kind; thus in summary the material (elemental) projection (<s>sarga</s>) is stated // ISk_53 //
107: Upwards there is an abundance of <s>Sattva</s>, and at the root (below) an abundance of <s>Tamas</s> is the projection,
108: in the middle, an abundance of <s>Rajas</s>, extending from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a pillar (a mere clod or plant) // ISk_54 //
109: Here the conscious <s>Puruṣa</s> obtains suffering caused by old age and death,
110: therefore, because of the non-cessation of the subtle mark-body (<s>liṅga</s>), suffering (is to be explained) in summary // ISk_55 //
111: Thus this undertaking, produced by <s>Prakṛti</s>, extends from the Great (<s>Mahad</s>) down to the elements as its domain,
112: for the sake of the release of each <s>Puruṣa</s>, an undertaking whose end is for another, as if (it were) for its own sake // ISk_56 //
113: Just as milk, being unintelligent, proceeds for the sake of the growth of the calf,
114: so does <s>Pradhāna</s> (<s>Prakṛti</s>) proceed for the sake of the release of the <s>Puruṣa</s> // ISk_57 //
115: Just as people engage in actions for the sake of the cessation of eagerness (curiosity, anxious expectancy),
116: so too the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) engages for the sake of the release of the <s>Puruṣa</s> // ISk_58 //
117: Just as a dancing girl, having shown the performance of the stage, withdraws from the dance,
118: so <s>Prakṛti</s>, having made herself manifest to the <s>Puruṣa</s>, withdraws // ISk_59 //
119: By manifold means, being helpful to the non-helping (non-agent) man (<s>puṃs</s>, i.e., <s>Puruṣa</s>),
120: being possessed of <s>guṇa</s>s for the sake of one without <s>guṇa</s>s, being existent for the sake of one that is (merely) existent, she (Prakṛti) acts for his sake, though that (sake) is purposeless (to herself) // ISk_60 //
121: My view is this: nothing is more delicate (subtle and considerate) than <s>Prakṛti</s>,
122: who, once seen as ‘I have been seen,’ does not again come to the sight of the <s>Puruṣa</s> // ISk_61 //
123: Therefore no one is bound, nor is anyone released, nor does anyone transmigrate,
124: it is <s>Prakṛti</s], resting on various supports, that transmigrates, is bound, and is released // ISk_62 //
125: With seven forms, in this way, <s>Prakṛti</s> binds herself by herself,
126: and that very (Prakṛti), with a single form, effects release for the sake of the <s>Puruṣa</s> // ISk_63 //
127: Thus, from practice regarding the principles (tattva-abhyāsa), ‘I am not,’ ‘this is not mine,’ ‘I am not this’—completely,
128: through non-misperception there arises knowledge that is pure and solitary // ISk_64 //
129: By that (knowledge) the <s>Puruṣa</s>, being established as a spectator, at ease (in himself), sees <s>Prakṛti</s>, whose production has ceased, who, because of the purpose being accomplished, has ceased from (her) seven forms,
130: like a spectator (he views her), remaining self-possessed // ISk_65 //
131: Through the attainment of right knowledge, when virtue and the rest (dharma, etc.) no longer obtain as causes,
132: he remains, by the force of residual impressions, with body sustained, like the whirling of a wheel // ISk_67 //
133: When the body breaks up, since his purpose has been accomplished and <s>Pradhāna</s> has ceased,
134: he attains isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) that is absolute and ultimate—both indeed // ISk_68 //
135: This knowledge of the <s>Puruṣa</s>’s purpose, profound (esoteric), was taught by the supreme seer,
136: where the abiding, arising, and dissolution of beings are contemplated // ISk_69 //
137: The sage gave this foremost purifier, out of compassion, to <s>Āsuri</s>,
138: and <s>Āsuri</s> to <s>Pañcaśikha</s>; and by him the system (tantra) was made abundant (widely promulgated) // ISk_70 //
139: Received through a succession of disciples, this (teaching) was also abbreviated by <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s> for the noble-minded,
140: having rightly understood the established doctrine (siddhānta) // ISk_71 //
141: The topics that are in the Seventy (verses) are indeed the topics of the entire sixty-tantra (i.e., the whole tradition),
142: devoid of anecdotes and free from refutations of others’ views // ISk_72 //
143: Therefore this scripture, seen in compendium, is not deficient in meaning,
144: and it is like a reflection transferred from the larger form of the treatise, as in a mirror // ISk_73 //
